Sell Your Rolex Watch in Los Angeles
Rolex is one of the most recognized names in the luxury watch resale market, but the value of one Rolex can differ significantly from another.

When evaluating a Rolex, relevant factors can include the model, reference number, production period, condition, dial, bracelet, materials, originality, box and papers, service history, and current demand for that particular configuration.
Popular Rolex collections can include models such as the Submariner, Daytona, GMT-Master II, Datejust, Day-Date, Explorer, Yacht-Master, and others.
If you have the original Rolex box, warranty card, papers, receipt, service records, or extra bracelet links, bring them with the watch.

We Buy More Than Rolex

Luxury watch value extends well beyond Rolex. We also evaluate watches from other desirable manufacturers, including Cartier, Audemars Piguet, Patek Philippe, Omega, Breitling, and other luxury brands based on current market demand.

Depending on the watch, important factors may include the specific collection, reference number, case material, dial configuration, movement, condition, originality, age, accessories, and current secondary-market demand.
What Determines the Value of a Luxury Watch?
There is no single price guide that determines what every luxury watch is worth. The value of a particular watch depends on several characteristics working together.
Brand and Model
Certain manufacturers, collections, and references have stronger secondary-market demand than others.
Reference Number
The exact reference can identify important differences between watches that may initially look very similar.
Condition
Case, bracelet, crystal, dial, bezel, movement, and overall wear can affect desirability and value.
Originality
Original components can matter to collectors. Replacement or aftermarket components may influence an evaluation depending on the watch.
Materials
Stainless steel, gold, platinum, two-tone construction, diamonds, and other materials can affect the value of a watch.
Box and Papers
Original warranty cards, certificates, boxes, receipts, manuals, hang tags, service records, and extra links can be helpful when evaluating provenance and completeness.
Current Market Demand
Luxury watch resale markets change. Demand for specific brands, models, references, dial configurations, sizes, and materials can influence what buyers are willing to pay.
How We Evaluate a Luxury Watch

A luxury watch evaluation can involve examining identifying characteristics of the watch, including its case, dial, bracelet, movement when appropriate, reference information, materials, condition, and other details.

The purpose is to understand exactly what watch is being presented and the factors relevant to its current resale market. Some watches may require additional authentication or research before an evaluation can be completed.
What Should I Bring When Selling My Watch?
The watch
Original box, if available
Warranty card or papers, if available
Original purchase receipt, if available
Service records
Extra bracelet links
Additional straps or accessories originally supplied with the watch
Relevant documentation
Do not worry if you no longer have every accessory. Bring the watch and whatever documentation or accessories remain, and we can determine what information is relevant during the evaluation.
Selling a Luxury Watch Locally vs. Online
Owners have several options when selling a luxury watch, including a direct local buyer, online marketplace, consignment company, or auction house.
Direct Local Watch Buyer
A local direct buyer allows the watch to be examined in person and gives the owner an opportunity to consider an item-specific offer without first shipping the watch to an unknown destination.
Online Marketplace
Selling directly to another consumer may require creating a listing, photographing the watch, communicating with buyers, handling payment, shipping, returns, and platform requirements.
Consignment
With consignment, the watch is generally marketed to another purchaser before the owner receives proceeds. Fees and timelines vary by company.
Auction
Auctions may be appropriate for certain rare or collectible watches, but fees, reserves, schedules, and results vary depending on the auction house and specific watch.
Compare the Final Offer for Your Actual Watch
When comparing luxury watch buyers, an early estimate is not necessarily the same thing as the final offer for the actual watch.
The watch’s exact reference, condition, originality, accessories, and other characteristics may not be fully known until the watch is examined.
Before deciding where to sell, consider the final item-specific offer and ask how the buyer arrived at the valuation.

Frequently Asked Questions About Selling Luxury Watches in Los Angeles
Where can I sell a luxury watch in Los Angeles?

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds evaluates luxury watches at our Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District location. Bring your watch and any available box, papers, receipts, service history, or accessories for an in-person evaluation.
Can I sell a Rolex without the box and papers?

You can still bring a Rolex for evaluation if you no longer have the original box or papers. Documentation and accessories can be helpful, but the watch itself and its specific characteristics are central to the evaluation.
What determines how much my Rolex is worth?
Factors can include the exact model and reference, condition, production period, materials, dial configuration, bracelet, originality, box and papers, service history, and current market demand.
Do you buy watches besides Rolex?

Yes. We evaluate luxury watches from brands including Cartier, Audemars Piguet, Patek Philippe, Omega, Breitling, and other desirable manufacturers, depending on the specific watch and current market demand.
Should I service or polish my watch before selling it?

Not necessarily. Before paying for service or polishing, it can be useful to have the watch evaluated in its current condition. On collectible watches, originality can be important, and unnecessary polishing may not always be desirable.
Does having the original box and papers matter?
Original documentation and accessories can help establish completeness and provenance. Their impact varies depending on the particular watch, model, age, and market.
Can I sell an older or vintage luxury watch?
Potentially, yes. Age alone does not determine value. Brand, reference, rarity, originality, condition, movement, history, and collector demand may all be relevant.
How do I compare offers from watch buyers?

Compare the final offer for your actual watch and ask what factors were considered. Preliminary estimates may change after the watch’s exact reference, condition, originality, and accessories are verified.
Do I need an appointment?

contact page
or call
to arrange your visit and confirm availability.
See our

Understanding Your Diamond Before You Sell
Selling a GIA Diamond in Los Angeles

A GIA grading report can provide important information about a diamond, including its carat weight, color, clarity, cut grade when applicable, measurements, proportions, and identifying characteristics.

If your diamond has its original GIA report, bring the report with you. We can use the grading information together with an inspection of the actual diamond and current market conditions when evaluating the stone.

A grading report does not by itself determine the amount a buyer will pay. Two diamonds with similar laboratory grades can have different resale demand and market values depending on characteristics such as shape, measurements, cut quality, fluorescence, condition, and current buyer demand.
How Is a Diamond’s Value Determined?
There is no single price-per-carat number that accurately values every diamond. Several characteristics work together to influence resale value.
Carat Weight

A diamond’s carat weight measures its weight, but larger diamonds do not simply increase in value at the same rate per carat. Size thresholds, quality, shape, and market demand can significantly affect value.
Cut
Cut and proportions affect how effectively a diamond reflects light and can influence both appearance and market desirability.
Color
For many colorless diamonds, less visible body color can affect grading and market value. Fancy-color diamonds are evaluated differently.
Clarity
Clarity considers inclusions and blemishes, including their size, number, position, and visibility.
Other important factors can include diamond shape, measurements, fluorescence, laboratory report, condition, brand or setting, and current wholesale and resale demand.
Sell Your Diamond Engagement Ring in Los Angeles

If you are selling a diamond engagement ring, we evaluate both the center diamond and the ring itself. Depending on the piece, factors such as additional diamonds, precious-metal content, designer branding, condition, and documentation may also affect the overall evaluation.

Bring any GIA reports, receipts, original boxes, designer documentation, or other paperwork you still have. These items are helpful when available, but they are not required for us to examine your jewelry.

Our goal is to make selling a diamond in Los Angeles straightforward and transparent. You can bring your diamond to our Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District location for an in-person evaluation and receive an offer based on the characteristics of your specific item and current market conditions.

Ask how the offer was determined and compare final, item-specific offers before deciding where to sell.
Local Diamond Buyer vs. Consignment or Auction
There are several ways to sell a diamond. The right choice depends on whether your priority is convenience, speed, or potentially waiting for a future buyer.
Direct Local Diamond Buyer
A direct buyer evaluates the diamond and can make an offer for the item. This allows the seller to decide whether to accept an offer without waiting for the jewelry to sell to another consumer.
Consignment
With consignment, the jewelry is generally listed for sale and the seller waits for another buyer to purchase it. Terms, fees, and timelines vary by company.
Auction
Auction may be appropriate for certain rare, important, or highly desirable pieces. Auction fees, timing, reserves, and results vary depending on the auction house and item.

Frequently Asked Questions About Selling Diamonds in Los Angeles
Where can I sell a diamond in Los Angeles?

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds evaluates diamonds at our location in the Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District. We evaluate loose diamonds, engagement rings, diamond jewelry, estate pieces, and GIA-graded diamonds.
Do I need a GIA certificate to sell my diamond?
No. A GIA report or other laboratory documentation is helpful when available, but you can still bring a diamond for evaluation without its original paperwork.
What determines how much my diamond is worth?
Diamond value can depend on carat weight, cut, color, clarity, shape, measurements, condition, laboratory grading, fluorescence, and current resale demand.
Do you buy loose diamonds?
Yes. We buy loose natural polished diamonds of any size and shape, as well as natural diamonds in engagement rings and other jewelry. We do not buy laboratory-grown or uncut diamonds.
Can I sell an engagement ring?
Yes. We evaluate diamond engagement rings and consider the center stone as well as relevant characteristics of the setting, additional stones, precious metals, branding, condition, and documentation.
Should I bring my GIA report?
Yes, if you have it. Bring the original GIA report and any other relevant documentation, receipts, boxes, or designer paperwork that may help identify the item.
How do I compare offers from diamond buyers?
Compare the final offer for your actual diamond and ask how the buyer determined the offer. Estimates given before physical inspection may change after the diamond’s characteristics are verified.
Is a diamond evaluation the same as an insurance appraisal?
Not necessarily. An insurance or replacement-value appraisal serves a different purpose from an offer to purchase a diamond in the current resale market.

children.text: How a complete-piece evaluation works
Identify the selection and its records
Show which pieces are available to sell and which documents belong to each item. Explain known repairs, altered settings, replaced stones or uncertain details.
Examine materials and condition

Metal content and weight, natural diamonds, construction, wear, maker markings and supporting records can affect the proposal. Ask what has been verified and what remains uncertain. Discuss any test that could mark or alter a piece before proceeding.
Review the purchase offer

Ask whether the offer considers the complete piece or primarily its materials, which items are included and whether deductions apply. An asking price seen online is not evidence that a comparable item sold for that amount.
A preliminary estimate is not the final offer

A phone description or photograph may support an initial estimate. The final in-person offer can differ after purity, weight, condition, authenticity, construction, stones and other characteristics are verified. Compare final net amounts for the same selection of pieces.
What to bring and what to preserve
Complete jewelry, pairs, matching sets and detached components.
Available receipts, reports, prior appraisals, repair records and original boxes, matched to the correct item.
Your own inventory and photographs, with uncertain details identified.
A clear list of pieces you are considering selling and pieces you plan to keep.
The identification and ownership documents confirmed when arranging the visit.
Do not polish, dismantle or discard components solely to prepare a sale. A signed or antique piece may need consideration as a complete object before treating it as scrap. Our
estate jewelry inventory guide
explains how to organize the collection.
Purchase offer or formal appraisal?

A current purchase offer states what a buyer proposes to pay for specified items under stated terms. An appraisal for insurance, estate administration or tax documentation has a different purpose. Confirm the requirements with the professional requesting that document; a buyer’s informal evaluation may not satisfy them.
Before selling for an estate or another person, establish who has authority to make the decision and confirm the documents needed. Read our
inherited jewelry documentation guide
Decide what to keep and compare the same items

You can identify only the pieces you are considering selling. Separate financial considerations from sentimental decisions and ask for terms for that exact selection. A historical retail receipt or insurance replacement figure is not a promised resale payment.
Cash, bank wire and business check are available for agreed purchases. Confirm the payment method and timing before accepting. Our guides to
comparing estate jewelry purchase offers
and
deciding whether to sell inherited jewelry
can help you prepare questions.
Questions about selling inherited and antique jewelry
Where can I sell inherited jewelry in Los Angeles?
Contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014. Call 310-663-1340 to describe the pieces and arrange an in-person purchase evaluation in the Downtown Jewelry District.
Is every piece of estate jewelry an antique?

No. Estate jewelry refers to previously owned pieces; inherited describes how someone received them. Neither description establishes age. An antique-style design also does not prove when a piece was made. Keep any records and describe uncertain details as unknown.
Can I bring jewelry if I do not know the stones or maker?

Yes, describe what you have when arranging a visit. Bring complete pieces and any records rather than guessing their materials or origin. Acceptance and an offer depend on the actual items and our buying scope.
Should I clean or repair antique jewelry before selling?
Keep the pieces intact and ask before cleaning, polishing, repairing or removing stones. Alterations can affect markings, surfaces, settings and other evidence needed to evaluate a complete piece.
Do I need a formal appraisal before asking for a purchase offer?

A purchase evaluation and a formal appraisal have different purposes. Bring any report you already have. If a document is needed for estate administration, insurance or another purpose, confirm its requirements with the professional requesting it.
Does an old appraisal determine the price I will receive?

No. The report’s date, purpose and description matter, and an insurance replacement figure is not a guaranteed resale payment. A current offer depends on the inspected item and the proposed purchase terms.
Can I sell only part of an inherited collection?

Identify the pieces you are considering selling and keep those you want to retain separate. Request an offer for that exact selection, and confirm your authority to sell before agreeing to a transaction.
Can a phone estimate change after the jewelry is examined?

Yes. A preliminary discussion relies on the description or photographs available. The final in-person offer can change after materials, purity, weight, condition, authenticity, construction and other characteristics are verified.

Can I sell an item bought in another country?

Which gemstones do you buy?

Can color prove a gemstone’s origin?

children.text: Heavy gold · Natural diamonds
Cuban links, with or without diamonds
Bring your heavy chains, bracelets and complete jewelry pieces. We consider the gold and any natural diamonds as part of the evaluation, including substantial pieces and larger collections.
Explore the gold bracelet guide
Understand the metal
10K, 14K, 18K, 22K and 24K gold

Karat describes the proportion of gold in an alloy. It is different from the carat weight used for diamonds. A stamp helps identify a piece, but plating, solder, repairs and mixed components can affect what is present.

cells: A higher gold proportion, still an alloy
Confirm the stated fineness and actual item

children.text: These are purity references, not prices or guaranteed test results. Gold-plated and gold-filled items differ from solid karat gold. See the
World Gold Council's explanation of gold purity
and our
14K gold value guide
An item-specific offer
How is a cash-for-gold offer determined?

For scrap gold, a useful starting point is the weight of the gold-bearing metal multiplied by its verified gold proportion and a current pure-gold price per unit of weight. This estimates metal value; it is not a guaranteed purchase price.
Spot gold is a market reference for gold itself. Jewelry's total weight may include stones, springs or other non-gold parts. Keep grams and troy ounces consistent when comparing calculations. Our
gold valuation guide
explains the distinction.

A purchase offer can differ from theoretical metal value because of recovery or refining costs, resale potential, market conditions and the buyer's margin. Designer provenance, collectible coin features and natural diamonds need separate consideration. Ask for the final net amount and the factors behind it.
Identify and examine the items
Markings, construction, maker details and condition help establish what is being evaluated. A photograph or receipt can assist but does not replace inspecting the piece.
Check purity and weight
Ask how purity is tested, which parts are included in the weight and whether stones or non-gold components affect the calculation. Mixed karats should not be treated as one assumed purity.
Review the purchase terms
Compare the offer, any deductions and payment arrangements. A retail replacement appraisal, an online asking price and a purchase offer serve different purposes.
What should you know about gold testing?

Evaluation may involve reading hallmarks, examining construction and choosing a testing method suited to the item. X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analyzes metal composition, but plating can affect the result. Acid or touchstone testing uses a sample or streak. Neither a marking nor one surface reading should be treated as the whole evaluation.

Ask which method will be used on your piece and whether it could leave a mark or require a sample. Discuss that first, especially for collectible coins, inherited jewelry or signed pieces. Call before visiting if you have testing concerns.

and
how plating can affect XRF results
Compare estimates carefully
A phone estimate can change after inspection

A preliminary phone or photo estimate uses details that have not yet been verified. The final in-person offer may be higher or lower after purity, weight, condition, authenticity, stones, maker details and other characteristics are checked. Market prices can also move before your visit.
Ask what assumptions an estimate uses, what remains to be checked and whether the amount is the final net purchase offer. There is no obligation to sell simply because you request an evaluation.

Missing paperwork does not establish that an item has no value. Bring what you have. Do not clean collectible coins, remove gemstones or repair jewelry solely for the evaluation without discussing it first.

Questions about selling gold in Los Angeles
Where can I sell gold in Los Angeles?
Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds evaluates gold at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, in the Downtown Jewelry District. Call 310-663-1340 to arrange a visit and discuss your items.
Can I sell broken jewelry or scrap gold?
Yes. We buy broken gold chains, damaged jewelry, single earrings and mixed scrap gold. An offer depends on the verified metal content and other characteristics of the actual items.
Does 18K gold always receive a higher offer than 14K?

18K has a higher nominal gold proportion per gram, but the offer also depends on weight, verified purity, stones, maker, condition and other features. A lighter 18K piece need not be worth more than a heavier 14K piece.
Do you buy gold coins and bullion?
We buy gold coins, including collections. Keep their holders and paperwork. Call ahead about bars or other bullion to confirm the format and quantity can be evaluated.
Can I sell inherited or designer gold jewelry?
Bring inherited and signed jewelry intact with available records. Discuss ownership authority when relevant. Maker, provenance, condition and stones may matter beyond gold content.
Will I receive the spot price for my jewelry?

Spot price is a reference for gold, not a guaranteed jewelry purchase price. Actual metal weight, purity, costs and other resale characteristics affect the offer. Ask for an explanation of the final net amount.
Why might my phone estimate differ from the final offer?

A phone estimate relies on unverified details. Purity, weight, authenticity, condition and other characteristics are checked in person; market conditions may also change. Compare the final offer after those checks.
Should I remove diamonds before selling gold jewelry?

Bring the complete piece first. Removing stones may damage jewelry or discard useful information. Our diamond buying covers natural, cut and polished diamonds; ask how the gold and eligible stones are considered together.
